facts.reason: Reconciliation is required for every closure but alone cannot establish a route.
Reconciliation and handover are common necessities; class-specific route conditions and an inactive hold are also required.
Settlement is necessary for routine closure, not for the exception route retained by CR-17.
Current exception routes retain the waiver and permit either completed audit or independent second inspection.
These new May 2 cases use the current receiving-lead definition, not the archived driver-signature card.
The field points to absent SI-9; no supplied authoritative definition maps Y to cleared settlement.
Neither a signed paid_at definition nor the migration mapping is supplied.
Arithmetic contribution alone is not evidence of a causal mechanism.
Closure does not establish payment authorization; payment is governed separately.
CR-17 changes only the audit alternative and expressly retains the waiver.
Receipt and posting describe distinct bank and ledger events, which can occur on different dates.
An active hold forbids closure even with a complete positive route.

decisions.reason: Routine reconciliation, handover and settlement are true and hold is false.
Routine settlement is unavailable; unmapped Y cannot establish it, and the exception route cannot substitute.
Exception common prerequisites and waiver are true; independent inspection supplies the current alternative, with no hold. Settlement is not required.
Exception waiver and audit establish the route with common prerequisites and inactive hold; inspection is not also required.
Explicitly false waiver defeats both current exception alternatives, regardless of audit, inspection or settlement.
True active hold prohibits closure despite complete routine positive conditions.
Routine positive conditions are established, but unavailable hold status prevents allowance without establishing prohibition.
Audit is false while independent inspection is unavailable; the inspection alternative remains unresolved, not defeated.
Both audit and independent inspection are explicitly false, defeating all exception routes.
Authoritative handover validity is false; a driver signature and archived card cannot satisfy the current requirement.
Routine cleared settlement is unavailable; receipt and posting dates identify events but do not attest cleared settlement.
Reconciliation is explicitly false and is necessary for every closure.
Independent inspection establishes one exception alternative with waiver and common prerequisites; unknown audit is immaterial and hold is false.
Completed audit establishes one exception alternative with waiver and common prerequisites; unknown inspection is immaterial and hold is false.
Routine settlement is explicitly false; exception waiver and audit do not authorize a routine route.
Necessary handover validity is unavailable, not false; remaining routine conditions do not resolve it.
